metadata.remarks: Consumers of this file should refer to the [Essentials OSCAL NS 1.0](#c1350084-c4c2-5447-affd-185f1ef2f6c2) page for information regarding the Essentials specific representation used in this OSCAL file.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data) are continually and centrally identified and documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintain current records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A maintained record of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets has not been established.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: There is no defined process for identifying, recording, reviewing and updating asset records.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Asset records are maintained, but identified omissions, inaccuracies or newly discovered assets are not triaged and addressed within the timeframes or tolerances defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A process to update the asset inventory runs on a schedule but the results are not reconciled or updated within a period defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: At each scheduled review or update, records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets are complete and accurate within the tolerances defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A defined process identifies changes and newly discovered assets between scheduled reviews, and ensures that records are reviewed, reconciled and updated within timeframes commensurate with the associated cyber security risk.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are planned, designed, developed, tested, deployed, maintained and decommissioned according to their business criticality ratings and security and resilience requirements using Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Design systems securely to provide visibility, enforce authorised access, protect data, minimise required and default privileges, limit exposed services and remove unnecessary functionality.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Systems are deployed with default configurations and no evidence of security design considerations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Unnecessary services, protocols or functionality remain enabled with no documented rationale.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Security telemetry is not enabled or is not considered as part of system design.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Security is considered during system design but not consistently applied across all assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Some unnecessary services have been disabled but a systematic review has not been completed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Security telemetry is partially enabled but gaps in coverage exist.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Systems are designed and deployed with exposed services limited, required and default permissions minimised, data protections in place, authorised access enforced, and only required functionality enabled.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Security telemetry is enabled by default.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Evidence exists that security design decisions are recorded and reviewed during system changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secure build and deployment processes to enforce controls consistently across systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No controlled build or deployment process exists for applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Changes to systems are applied ad hoc, without any version control, testing or approval.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A controlled deployment process exists but is not consistently followed for all changes.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Version control is in place but pre-deployment security verification is not performed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A controlled build and deployment process is in place and consistently followed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Configuration changes are subject to version control, testing and approval before deployment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Security controls are confirmed to be implemented consistently across systems following deployment processes.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Cyber supply chains supporting systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are secure, resilient and support effective and coordinated cyber security incident response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Assess the integrity and authenticity of software, components and updates before use, and verify provenance where suitable supplier evidence is available.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No verification of software, component or update integrity or authenticity is performed before introduction into systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Verification outcomes are not recorded or available for review.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where verification cannot be performed, no compensating control or remediation paths are documented.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Verification is performed for some categories of software but not consistently across operating systems, applications, firmware and dependencies.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Integrity or provenance checks are performed, but they do not provide sufficient assurance for all software, components or updates.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Verification outcomes are recorded for some software, components or updates prior to being introduced into systems, but not consistently.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Compensating controls exist for some unverifiable components but are not formally approved or time-bound.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Verification of integrity and provenance is performed for software, components and updates across all relevant categories, and provenance is verified where suitable supplier evidence is available.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Verification uses one or more mechanisms appropriate to the software, component, update and source to provide reliable assurance of integrity and provenance.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Verification outcomes are recorded and available for review.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where verification cannot be performed, compensating controls are applied, exceptions are time-bound and remediation paths are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use vendor advisories and threat intelligence to maintain awareness of supplier, product and component exposure to compromise, and act within timeframes proportionate to the risk.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No monitoring is performed for indicators of supply chain compromise affecting software, components or services in use.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Vendor security notifications and threat advisories are not reviewed or actioned.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: When supply chain compromise is identified, neither containment nor investigation is performed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Supply chain compromise events are integrated into neither incident response nor risk management.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Monitoring occurs but does not draw on relevant threat intelligence sources or does not cover all in-scope systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Notifications and advisories are reviewed but exposure assessment and response are not conducted in a timely manner.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Containment occurs but investigation for evidence of exploitation is not consistently undertaken.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Some integration exists but findings are not reflected in the risk register or incident response procedures.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Monitoring covers software, components and services in use, drawing on relevant threat intelligence sources.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Vendor security notifications and threat advisories are reviewed, exposure is assessed and response actions are initiated within defined timeframes.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Identified supply chain compromises are responded to in timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Supply chain compromise events are integrated with incident response and reflected in the risk register.

groups.title: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Robust and secure identity, credential and access management is used to establish, maintain and control access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) and to support effective detection of identity and credential misuse.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identify and disable or remove default and unused accounts regularly, permitting exceptions only where the account is documented, justified, hardened and monitored.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No review of default or unused accounts has been conducted within the review period defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Default vendor accounts remain enabled on production systems without appropriate documentation, justification, hardening and monitoring in place for their use.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No process exists to identify accounts that have not authenticated within a defined period.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A review has been conducted but does not cover all assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Default accounts have been identified but some remain enabled without documented justification.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Unused accounts are identified but remediation is incomplete or delayed beyond defined timeframes.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A review of accounts has been completed within the defined review period covering all assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Default accounts are disabled or have approved justification for remaining active, with appropriate monitoring and compensating controls for their use in place.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Accounts that show no evidence of use, other than approved emergency access accounts, are identified and either disabled or removed in accordance with defined timeframes.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Credentials from Password Stores

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Store authentication keys, secrets and tokens in approved secure repositories with access controls, including MFA.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credentials are stored in plaintext, spreadsheets, shared drives or other unapproved locations as standard practice.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No approved secure repository is in use to store authentication keys, secrets and tokens.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access to credential stores is neither controlled nor audited.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access controls such as MFA are not enabled for authentication to secure repositories.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: An approved secure repository is in use but does not cover all authentication keys, secrets and tokens within scope.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access controls for secure repositories are in place but access logging is not enabled or not reviewed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: MFA is enforced for some, but not all, applicable users, repositories or authentication pathways, and the remaining exceptions are documented and subject to remediation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Authentication keys, secrets and tokens within scope are stored in approved secure repositories, with any authorised exceptions documented, risk-assessed and managed in accordance with organisationally defined requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access to secure repositories is restricted using attribute or role-based access controls, MFA is enforced for all applicable authentication pathways, and access is logged and reviewed and investigated where necessary.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use phishing-resistant MFA for users authenticating to systems, including from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Phishing-resistant MFA is not enforced for interactive user authentication to systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: MFA is deployed but uses non-phishing-resistant methods, such as SMS, voice, or push-only authentication instead of phishing-resistant MFA.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No access policies differentiate between trusted and untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access from untrusted, external or high-risk locations is permitted without MFA, or with non-phishing-resistant MFA.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Phishing-resistant MFA is deployed for some but not all systems within scope.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access policies exist but do not cover all organisationally defined high-risk location categories.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Exceptions or alternative authentication pathways allow routine or recurring authentication without phishing-resistant MFA, or emergency access arrangements are not adequately restricted, monitored, tested or reviewed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for all routine interactive user authentication to systems within scope.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for routine authentication attempts from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Customer-facing services provide a phishing-resistant MFA option for authentication.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Emergency access arrangements are periodically tested and reviewed to confirm that they remain operational, appropriately protected and limited to their intended purpose. Credentials or authentication factors used for emergency access are securely managed and are not used for routine administration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Disable legacy authentication protocols or, where this is not feasible, restrict and monitor their use, apply compensating controls and establish a time-bound decommissioning plan.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce modern authentication controls remain enabled and in active use without restriction.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No assessment has been conducted to identify which legacy authentication protocols are in use within the environment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Authentication mechanisms transmitting credentials in cleartext or using weak cryptographic primitives remain enabled and no action has been taken to disable them.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where legacy protocols are retained, no compensating controls, no monitoring and no decommissioning timelines are in place.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Legacy authentication protocols have been identified and are partially restricted but some remain enabled across systems within scope without justification.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: An assessment has been conducted but does not cover all in-scope systems, or the inventory of legacy protocols in use is not maintained.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Some weak authentication mechanisms have been disabled but others remain enabled without documented justification or remediation plan.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Compensating controls exist for some retained legacy protocols but monitoring is inconsistent or decommissioning timelines are not defined.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Legacy authentication protocols that cannot enforce modern authentication controls have been identified and disabled across systems within scope, excluding documented and risk accepted exceptions.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: An assessment of legacy authentication protocol use has been conducted across in-scope systems and the inventory is maintained.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where retention is necessary, compensating controls are applied and decommissioning timelines are recorded and tracked.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Ongoing use of legacy authentication protocols is regularly risk reviewed, accepted and recorded in the organisation’s risk register.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure that user, machine, system and service account credentials are unique per system or account, particularly in high-privilege contexts.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Local administrator credentials are shared across the device fleet, or service or privileged account credentials are routinely reused across systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credential uniqueness is not enforced for applicable user, machine, system or service identities.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credential uniqueness has not been addressed in high-privilege contexts, including domain administration, cloud administration or automation platforms.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where credential uniqueness cannot be enforced, neither compensating controls nor remediation paths are in place.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Local administrator credential uniqueness has been implemented for some device populations but coverage is incomplete across the device fleet.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A technical mechanism is in place but applies to only a subset of credential types or systems within scope.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credential uniqueness has been addressed in some high-privilege contexts but gaps remain in others.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Compensating controls exist for some shared credentials but monitoring is inconsistent or remediation plans do not exist.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credentials for applicable local administrative accounts are unique to each system or account.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credential uniqueness is consistently enforced for applicable user, machine, system and service identities.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Credential uniqueness is enforced consistently in high-privilege contexts, with managed identities or equivalent capabilities used in preference to shared static credentials wherever feasible.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where uniqueness cannot be enforced, compensating controls are applied, the use of the shared credentials is monitored, and a remediation plan exists.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Users are granted the minimum access to systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) required to undertake their duties or functions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Periodically review and update access privileges in alignment with current roles, duties and business requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access privileges are not reviewed against current roles, duties and business requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access reviews do not identify privileges that are no longer required.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access privileges are not updated when personnel roles, duties or business requirements change.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access privileges are not mapped to roles, duties and business requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access reviews are conducted for some accounts or systems, but coverage is incomplete.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Reviews identify excessive or obsolete privileges, but updates are incomplete or not completed within timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A process to review access privileges exists but only occurs on an ad hoc basis.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Some access privileges are mapped to roles, duties and business requirements, but not all.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access privileges for all applicable accounts and systems are reviewed within a cycle defined by the organisation and aligned with current roles, duties and business requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Privileges identified as excessive or obsolete are removed or updated within timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Review outcomes and resulting access changes are documented and available as evidence.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access privileges are mapped to current roles, duties and business requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Grant only authorised administrative roles permissions to create, modify or delete accounts and roles, and access privileged functions or applications.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Non-administrative users can create, modify or delete accounts or roles.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Delegated permissions are broad and have not been audited.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Permissions are restricted to administrative roles but some delegated permissions are broader than required.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approval workflows exist for some high-impact changes but not all.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Only designated administrative roles can create, modify or delete accounts and roles.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Delegated permissions are audited and scoped to the minimum required.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approval workflows are enforced for high-impact identity and access changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Provision user, administrative and non-person accounts with only the minimum access and privileges required to perform defined operational functions.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Accounts are provisioned with broad default permissions that exceed operational requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative and day-to-day user functions share the same account, with no separate privileged accounts.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Minimum privilege provisioning is defined but not consistently applied to all account types.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative accounts are separated from user accounts but some exceptions exist without documented justification.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: All accounts are provisioned with documented minimum permissions aligned to defined operational functions.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Separate accounts are allocated for privileged and day-to-day functions, and controls prevent privileged use from day-to-day context.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Non-person and service accounts are scoped to their specific integration requirements.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are administered in a secure, accountable and auditable manner.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensure administrative activities can only be performed from dedicated and hardened environments that are isolated from unprivileged user workloads.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative access to systems is routinely performed from standard user devices without additional controls to protect the administrative session.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No dedicated or hardened administrative environment exists.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Exceptions to the use of dedicated administrative environments are neither identified nor assessed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A dedicated administrative environment has been established, but administrative access is not consistently routed through it.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative endpoints have been hardened, but unprivileged user workloads or unnecessary functions remain accessible.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Exceptions are documented, but their justification, risk acceptance, compensating controls or review arrangements are incomplete or inconsistently applied.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative sessions originate from dedicated and hardened administrative environments that are isolated from unprivileged user workloads. Where this cannot be technically enforced, exceptions are documented, risk-assessed, formally accepted and protected by compensating controls.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative environments are hardened and restricted to the functions required for authorised administration.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Exceptions are limited to systems or services that cannot support administration through a dedicated environment, are periodically reviewed and are removed when the technical limitation no longer applies.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Use Alternate Authentication Material
Mitigated technique: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Enforce explicit session establishment controls before privileged actions are permitted, including the use of time-bound privilege grants.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Privileged access is standing and does not require explicit activation or time-bound grants, excluding approved break-glass and emergency access accounts.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No re-authentication or step-up authentication is required before privileged sessions.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Time-bound access is implemented for some privileged roles but standing access remains for others.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Session duration limits exist but are not consistently enforced or are set excessively long.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Time-bound privilege grants are enforced for applicable privileged roles, with defined maximum session durations and approved emergency access arrangements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Re-authentication or step-up authentication is required before privilege activation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: All privilege activations are logged with activating user, role and timeframes.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools
Mitigated technique: Create or Modify System Process

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Record all administrative or management actions that modify systems, configurations or controls, including the details of the associated user, timestamp and target.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative or management actions that modify systems, configurations or controls are not logged.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Logs do not capture sufficient detail to identify who made a change, when and to what target.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Logging is enabled and provides useful coverage, but does not cover all applicable administrative or management platforms.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Logs capture the administrator identity and action but lack detail on the target or change nature.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Comprehensive audit logging to capture all administrative or management actions is enabled on all platforms in scope.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Logs capture administrator identity, timestamp, target object and nature of change.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are securely configured to approved and maintained baselines, including by reducing attack surfaces and attack paths, with configurations continually monitored and consistently enforced.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Define approved configuration baselines, informed by vendor and industry hardening guidance, that disable or remove unnecessary services, insecure settings, and unsupported or weak communication protocols.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No documented configuration baseline exists for assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Systems are deployed with vendor defaults and no documented hardening has been applied.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A baseline exists but does not address all applicable asset types.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The baseline is documented but has not been reviewed or updated within the cycle defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The baseline exists but rationale for configuration decisions is not documented.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A documented and approved baseline exists for all applicable asset types.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The baseline disables or removes unnecessary services, insecure settings, and unsupported or weak communication protocols.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Configuration decisions are documented with rationale to support drift assessment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The baseline is reviewed and updated on a cycle defined by the organisation.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Command and Scripting Interpreter

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Deploy approved configuration baselines on systems, including infrastructure, operating systems and applications.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved baselines have not been applied to assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Baseline deployment has not been validated through technical assessment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved baselines have been implemented where available, but some relevant asset types are not covered by an approved baseline.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Deployment has occurred but validation through technical assessment is incomplete or not current.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved baselines have been deployed, but coverage for all applicable assets is inconsistent.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved baselines have been applied to all applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Deployment has been validated through technical assessment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Coverage metrics are available demonstrating deployment completeness.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Detect and respond to configuration drift using scheduled technical assessments and, where supported, automated monitoring, based on system criticality and change rate.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No mechanism exists to detect configuration drift from approved baselines.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Assessments to detect configuration drift have not been conducted within the review period defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Assessments do not systematically identify instances of configuration drift for assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Drift detection is in place but does not cover all applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Drift is detected but the remediation process is informal or response timeframes are not defined.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Automated configuration monitoring or regular technical assessments detect drift across the applicable assets, occurring at a frequency based on system criticality and change rate.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A documented remediation process exists with defined response timeframes aligned to severity.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Drift events are tracked to closure with evidence of remediation.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Vulnerabilities in systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are identified, documented, validated and prioritised for remediation or mitigation in a timely manner, with all remediation and mitigation actions verified for effectiveness.

Mitigated technique: Exploitation of Remote Services
Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Client Execution

parts.prose: Vulnerability scanning activities are not undertaken.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No routine vulnerability assessment activity has been conducted within a period defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Advisories for relevant software and configuration weaknesses for organisational assets are not reviewed and assessed for impact.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Vulnerability scanning is deployed but does not cover all applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Vulnerability scans are conducted but results are not reviewed and prioritised within timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Vulnerability scans are conducted but frequency is not regular enough to enable timely response.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Scanning covers software vulnerabilities but not configuration weaknesses.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Advisories for relevant software and configuration weaknesses for organisational assets are reviewed on an ad hoc basis, or only for some assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: All applicable assets are included in routine vulnerability scanning, and scanning frequency enables timely response.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Scanning covers both software vulnerabilities and configuration weaknesses.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Results are reviewed and prioritised within timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Advisories for relevant software and configuration weaknesses in all organisational assets are regularly reviewed and assessed for impact.

Mitigated technique: Exploitation of Remote Services

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Apply security patches or updates within defined risk-based timeframes or automatically where operational impact is low.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No defined patching timeframes exist for applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Patches are not applied or are applied on an ad hoc basis with no tracking.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Expected patching timeframes are defined by the organisation but are not consistently met.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Patches are applied but compensating controls are not documented where operational constraints prevent timely patching.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Patching coverage metrics exist but show significant gaps.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Risk-based patching timeframes defined by the organisation are in place and consistently met.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Patching is prioritised based on vulnerability severity, exposure and exploit availability.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where operational constraints prevent timely patching, compensating controls are documented and approved.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Patching coverage metrics account for all applicable assets, with any exclusions identified and formally risk accepted.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Automatic patching of assets is applied where available and the organisation has determined operational impact is low.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
Mitigated technique: Exploitation of Remote Services
Mitigated technique: Exploitation for Client Execution

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Remediate or mitigate vulnerabilities exceeding defined risk thresholds within defined timeframes based on exploitation, exposure, criticality, impact and compensating controls, and verify treatment effectiveness.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No risk thresholds are defined for vulnerability remediation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Vulnerabilities exceeding acceptable risk levels are not tracked or remediated.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Risk thresholds are defined but vulnerabilities exceeding them are not consistently remediated within defined timeframes.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Compensating controls are applied in some cases but are not formally documented or approved.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Risk thresholds defined by the organisation exist, and vulnerabilities exceeding them are remediated or have approved compensating controls within organisationally defined timeframes.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Remediation and mitigation actions are tracked to closure with verification that actions reduced the risk as intended.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The process is sustained, with historical data demonstrating consistent performance across organisationally defined reporting periods.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (operating systems and applications) only permit the execution of software that is supported, verified and authorised.

Mitigated technique: System Binary Proxy Execution

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Permit only supported, verified and organisation-authorised software to execute on systems, with exceptions minimised, formally risk accepted, time-bound, monitored and regularly reviewed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Unsupported, unverified or unauthorised software can execute without restriction.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The list of approved software does not exist.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Execution restriction controls are deployed but do not cover all applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The organisation maintains a list of approved software, but it has not been reviewed within timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Execution restrictions are in place but integrity verification of approved software is not performed.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Exceptions to execution restrictions are granted without formal approval or time-bounding.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Controls restrict execution to supported, organisation-authorised and integrity-verified software on all applicable assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The organisation maintains a list of approved software and reviews it within the timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Integrity of permitted software is verified using trusted mechanisms appropriate to the software and its source.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Exceptions are formally approved, documented, time-bound and reviewed on a regular cycle defined by the organisation.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Disable or Modify Tools
Mitigated technique: Command and Scripting Interpreter
Mitigated technique: System Binary Proxy Execution

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Restrict administrative and management tooling to approved software sets and executed from only authorised, known locations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No approved administrative toolset is defined.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No restrictions are placed on the location administrative tooling can be executed from.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No controls prevent unapproved administrative tools, including tools commonly used in post-compromise activity, from executing on managed assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: An approved toolset is defined but not consistently enforced across all assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative tooling is configured to execute from known locations, but privileged users can still run tooling from unapproved locations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Some unapproved administrative tools are blocked but enforcement gaps exist.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A defined and enforced approved toolset exists for administrative and management activities, and execution is limited to authorised, known locations.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Administrative and management tooling outside the approved set is blocked from execution, including from unauthorised locations.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are regularly backed up in a secure and proven manner, including through the validation of restoration capabilities.

links.text: Mitigated technique: Data Encrypted for Impact

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Back up important data, applications and settings on a defined schedule to secure, resilient storage protected by encryption and immutable, offline, logically isolated or equivalent controls.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No managed backup process exists for important data, applications and settings.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup storage is neither encrypted nor protected by immutable, offline, logically isolated or equivalent controls.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Important data, applications and settings are backed up, but backup schedules are not defined, do not cover all important assets, or are not consistently met.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backups are encrypted but no immutable, offline, logically isolated or equivalent resilience controls are consistently applied.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backups use immutable, offline, logically isolated or equivalent controls, but encryption is not consistently enforced.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: All important data, applications and settings are backed up according to schedules defined by the organisation and aligned with their recovery requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup schedules are monitored, and missed or unsuccessful backups are identified, investigated and remediated within timeframes defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup storage is encrypted and protected by immutable, offline, logically isolated or equivalent controls.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Isolate backup repositories from general user environments and production workloads, ensuring they are separated from primary systems to prevent unauthorised access, modification or deletion.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup repositories are accessible from the production environment or by production administrators.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Compromise of a system would provide a direct path to access, modify or delete its own backups.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup repositories are logically separated but use credentials managed by the same identity platform as production.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Isolation is implemented but has not been tested or validated.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup repositories are isolated from production environments and general user access.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access is controlled through credentials and administrative paths isolated from compromise of the primary identity environment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Isolation has been validated to confirm that compromise of a system does not provide access to backups.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conduct regular testing of backup and restoration procedures to ensure that backups are reliable and capable of meeting defined recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives.

parts.prose: No restoration test has been conducted within the test cycle defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No backup or restoration procedures exist.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Restoration testing has been conducted but does not cover all important assets.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Backup procedures exist but have never been tested.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Testing has been conducted but coverage is incomplete or some tests did not meet the expected recovery time or recovery point objectives.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Restoration testing covering important assets is conducted within the test cycle defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Testing validates that restoration meets the expected recovery time and recovery point objectives.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Test results are documented and gaps identified during testing are remediated.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Systems (infrastructure, operating systems and applications) are segmented into network zones based on business criticality and trust levels, with only authorised, controlled and monitored inbound and outbound communication paths between network zones permitted.

parts.name: statement

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Systems are deployed on shared or flat network segments with no segregation between functions or trust levels.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No access controls restrict network access from external or general user networks to in-scope systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Segmentation is documented or administratively defined but not enforced by technical controls.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Segmentation has not been validated through technical assessment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Network segmentation has been implemented but does not cover all in-scope systems, or segments are defined inconsistently.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Access controls exist between segments, but deny-by-default is not enforced, or some pathways are permitted without documented approval.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Technical enforcement is in place for some segments but relies on a single mechanism that does not provide meaningful isolation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Validation has been performed for some segments but not consistently across in-scope systems, or validation is out of date.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Pathways are reviewed, but findings are not actioned, or the review cycle is not defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Systems within scope are deployed in network segments defined according to function, criticality and trust level, with segmentation applied consistently.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Deny-by-default access controls are enforced between segments, with access from external and general user networks limited to documented and approved pathways.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Segmentation is enforced through network-layer technical controls that provide meaningful isolation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Segmentation has been validated through technical assessment with results documented and gaps remediated.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved pathways are reviewed on a regular cycle defined by the organisation, with unjustified pathways removed and changes reflected in the access control configuration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Limit lateral movement between, and within, network segments to explicitly approved pathways and services, based on business requirements and trust levels.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: No controls limit lateral movement between or within network segments.

parts.prose: Lateral movement is permitted by default across the environment, with restrictions applied only on an exception basis.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved pathways are not documented.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Lateral movement controls have not been validated through technical assessment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Pathways and services are not reviewed after initial approval.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Controls limit lateral movement between segments but no controls operate within segments.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Restrictions are applied to some pathways, but the default position remains permissive in parts of the environment.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved pathways are documented but documentation is out of date or incomplete.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Validation has been performed but does not cover all in-scope segments, or is out of date.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Pathways are reviewed, but findings are not actioned, or the review cycle is not defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Controls limit lateral movement both between and within segments, with deny-by-default applied at each boundary.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Pathways and services are explicitly approved based on documented business requirements and trust levels, with all other lateral movement denied.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Approved pathways are documented, reflect the current configuration and identify the business requirement and trust relationship justifying each.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Lateral movement controls have been validated through technical assessment with results documented and gaps remediated.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Pathways and services are reviewed on a regular cycle defined by the organisation, with unjustified pathways removed and the configuration updated to reflect approved changes.

parts.prose: Data communicated between different security domains for systems (infrastructure and applications) is controlled and subject to inspection and verification.

parts.prose: Alerts are generated but are not triaged or acted upon in a timely manner.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Outbound content inspection is deployed covering all applicable egress paths.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Rules are configured to detect unauthorised transfer of classified, regulated and high-value data.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Alerts are triaged and responded to within accepted risk timeframes defined by the organisation.

Mitigated technique: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol

parts.prose: Block outbound network connections to known malicious or untrusted destinations.

parts.name: item

parts.prose: Threat intelligence is used to inform block decisions for outbound connections, but updates are infrequent, manual or limited to a single source.

parts.prose: Categorisation is in place, but the categories blocked do not reflect the organisation’s risk position.

parts.prose: Controls are deployed and applied across in-scope systems, egress paths, services, and network boundaries.

parts.prose: Blocking decisions draw on current threat intelligence, with destination lists updated on a cycle defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Destination reputation, category and age are considered alongside threat intelligence, with category-based blocking aligned to the organisation’s risk position.

parts.prose: Inspect inbound content from external or untrusted sources to prevent delivery of malicious or unsafe content.

parts.prose: Inbound inspection is deployed but does not cover all applicable content channels.

parts.prose: Inbound content inspection covers all applicable content channels.

parts.prose: Detection signatures and rules are maintained and updated on a regular cycle defined by the organisation.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Blocked content is logged and available for review.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Current cyber threat intelligence is considered when implementing controls to prevent the delivery of malicious or unsafe content.

parts.prose: A requirement to complete training before access is granted exists but is not consistently enforced.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Completion records are maintained but show significant gaps in coverage.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Role-tailored training programs address the specific risks, data handling obligations and incident reporting requirements relevant to in-scope systems.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Completion records are maintained and demonstrate full coverage.

parts.prose: Security-relevant event logs and configuration changes for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are centrally collected, protected against unauthorised modification or deletion, and retained to support effective cyber security event detection and investigation.

parts.prose: Logs are protected against modification or deletion.

parts.prose: Log completeness has been validated against the expected log sources.

parts.prose: Baseline patterns of identity and credential access activities, privileged access activities, and remote access activities are established and maintained for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) to enable the detection of anomalous or unexpected behaviour.

parts.prose: Existing controls do not provide a reasonable capability to detect security-relevant patterns of legitimate software being used for malicious purposes.

parts.prose: Monitoring or equivalent analysis covers some priority tools, execution behaviours or applicable systems, but risk-significant coverage gaps exist.

parts.prose: Security-relevant execution telemetry is collected, but detection rules, behavioural analytics or equivalent analysis are incomplete or not consistently operational.

parts.prose: Alerts relating to anomalous or unexpected software execution are generated, but they are not consistently triaged and investigated within organisationally defined timeframes.

parts.prose: The organisation identifies the legitimate tools, utilities and execution behaviours that present heightened risk of malicious use within applicable systems.

parts.prose: Security-relevant telemetry and contextual information are analysed using detection rules, behavioural analytics or equivalent methods to identify anomalous or unexpected use of priority tools and utilities.

parts.prose: Detection coverage is periodically reviewed and adjusted in response to changes in applicable systems, threat intelligence, observed activity and the organisation’s risk profile.

parts.prose: Alerts are prioritised, triaged and investigated within timeframes defined according to their assessed security risk.

parts.prose: Logs are time-synchronised to the authoritative time source.
